trends.name: Defense Rearmament
trends.thesis: Russia's invasion of Ukraine (2022) broke three decades of European defense underinvestment; NATO's 2% (and now 3.5-5% roadmap) GDP commitments are structural, not cyclical. The Middle East/Iran axis (Gaza, Red Sea shipping disruption, direct Iran-Israel exchanges) has widened the buyer base beyond Europe and lifted energy-security spending (oil price volatility, LNG infrastructure) as a linked second-order effect.

sub_themes.name: Ammunition & Energetics
sub_themes.definition: Production of artillery and small-arms ammunition, propellants and explosive energetics for military resupply.

sub_themes.name: Sensors & Electronic Warfare
sub_themes.definition: Radar, signals-intelligence and electronic-warfare/jamming systems for military detection and countermeasures.

sub_themes.name: Drones & Counter-Drone
sub_themes.definition: Unmanned aerial systems for military reconnaissance/strike and the counter-drone systems that defend against them.

sub_themes.name: Military & Critical-Infrastructure Cyber
sub_themes.definition: Cybersecurity for defense networks, weapons platforms and critical national infrastructure against state-sponsored threats.

trends.name: Energy Security & Independence
trends.thesis: The 2022 European gas-supply shock and continued Middle East volatility (Strait of Hormuz risk, Red Sea shipping) pushed energy independence from a cost question to a security question: LNG terminal buildout, grid interconnects, nuclear restarts/SMRs, and strategic reserve policy are now priced as durable capex, not one-off crisis response.

scarcity.risk: Strait of Hormuz / Red Sea chokepoint disruption; long lead time on new terminal capacity

sub_themes.name: LNG Infrastructure & Shipping
sub_themes.definition: LNG export/import terminal buildout and the specialized carrier fleet that moves gas to replace pipeline dependency.

sub_themes.name: Grid Interconnects & Transmission
sub_themes.definition: High-voltage transmission and cross-border interconnect equipment enabling energy-security-driven grid buildout.

sub_themes.name: Nuclear Restarts & SMRs
sub_themes.definition: Restart of idled nuclear capacity and development of small modular reactors as dispatchable low-carbon energy-security supply.

trends.name: AI Compute Buildout
trends.thesis: Generative-AI training and inference demand is driving a multi-year capex cycle across compute (accelerators), power (data-center electricity demand growth outpacing grid buildout), cooling (liquid cooling displacing air as rack density rises), and networking. The trend is broadly still emerging- to-active: hyperscaler capex guidance keeps being revised upward.

scarcity.risk: Taiwan Strait geopolitical risk concentrates >90% of leading-edge capacity in a single contested region

sub_themes.name: AI Compute (Accelerators)
sub_themes.definition: GPUs and custom accelerators for training and inference of large-scale AI models.

sub_themes.name: Power Delivery & Grid Interconnect
sub_themes.definition: Data-center power infrastructure and grid interconnect equipment sized for AI-driven electricity demand growth.

sub_themes.name: Liquid Cooling & Thermal Management
sub_themes.definition: Liquid cooling systems displacing air cooling as AI rack power density rises.

sub_themes.name: Model & Application Layer
sub_themes.definition: Foundation-model providers and the application software built on top of them monetizing AI compute demand.

trends.name: Copper & Electrification
trends.thesis: Grid buildout (renewables interconnection, AI data-center power delivery, EV charging infrastructure) is copper-intensive at a moment when new mine supply is structurally lagging demand (permitting timelines of 10-15 years, declining ore grades at existing mines). This is a multi-decade structural deficit thesis, not a cyclical commodity trade.

scarcity.risk: Chile/Peru political and water-permitting risk; DRC governance and infrastructure risk

sub_themes.name: Mining & Concentrate Production
sub_themes.definition: Extraction of copper ore and production of copper concentrate at the primary mine level.

sub_themes.name: Smelting & Refining
sub_themes.definition: Conversion of copper concentrate into refined cathode copper.

sub_themes.name: Wire & Cable Manufacturing
sub_themes.definition: Manufacturing of copper wire and cable for grid, EV-charging and building electrification.

sub_themes.name: Grid Equipment (Transformers & Switchgear)
sub_themes.definition: Copper-intensive transformers and switchgear for grid interconnection and electrification buildout.

trends.name: Semiconductor Supply Chain
trends.thesis: Post-2020 chip-shortage policy response (US CHIPS Act, EU Chips Act, Japan and India subsidy programs) is reshoring and de-risking a supply chain that is otherwise extremely geographically concentrated, overlapping heavily with the AI-buildout trend at the leading edge but distinct at mature nodes (auto, industrial) where the reshoring thesis is strongest.

scarcity.risk: Single-supplier (ASML) chokepoint on the entire leading-edge industry

sub_themes.name: Leading-Edge Logic Fabrication
sub_themes.definition: Fabrication of leading-edge (<=5nm) logic chips concentrated in a handful of foundries.

sub_themes.name: Mature-Node Fabrication (Auto/Industrial)
sub_themes.definition: Fabrication of mature-node chips for automotive and industrial reshoring programs.

sub_themes.name: Fab Equipment & Materials
sub_themes.definition: Lithography, deposition and etch equipment and specialty materials required to build and run a fab.

sub_themes.name: Advanced Packaging & OSAT
sub_themes.definition: Advanced chip packaging (chiplets, 2.5D/3D stacking) and outsourced assembly/test services.

trends.name: Memory Cycle (DRAM/NAND)
trends.thesis: Memory is the classic boom-bust semiconductor sub-cycle, but the current up-cycle is amplified by AI-server HBM (high-bandwidth memory) demand, which draws capacity away from commodity DRAM and tightens the whole market. Treated as a distinct, faster-cycling trend from the structural AI-buildout and semiconductor trends above.

scarcity.risk: Two-supplier (SK Hynix, Samsung) concentration on the highest-margin AI-memory segment

sub_themes.name: Commodity DRAM
sub_themes.definition: Standard DRAM memory production for PCs, servers and mobile devices.

sub_themes.name: High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM)
sub_themes.definition: High-bandwidth memory stacked for AI accelerators, the highest-margin and most supply-constrained memory segment.

sub_themes.name: NAND Flash & Storage
sub_themes.definition: NAND flash memory production for SSDs and enterprise storage.

trends.name: Consumer Cyclicals — South Korea
trends.thesis: Illustrative country-specific consumer cycle: cap-weighted Korea index exposure is dominated by Samsung Electronics and a handful of mega-caps, so passive flows into "Korea growth" reach semiconductor/tech exposure first and structurally under-weight the domestic consumer names (retail, cosmetics, entertainment/content export) that benefit most from a won-driven consumption recovery. Kept as a template for other country-specific consumer trends to be added the same way.

sub_themes.name: Domestic Retail
sub_themes.definition: Department stores and domestic retail chains benefiting from a won-driven Korean consumption recovery.

sub_themes.name: Cosmetics & K-Beauty
sub_themes.definition: Korean cosmetics and personal-care brands benefiting from domestic consumption and export demand.

sub_themes.name: Entertainment & Content Export
sub_themes.definition: K-pop, streaming and entertainment-content companies monetizing Korean cultural export demand.

trends.name: Infrastructure Renewal
trends.thesis: Grid modernization, transport, and water infrastructure across the US and Europe is past its useful life (much of it built 1950s-1970s) at the same moment electrification and AI power demand require net-new grid capacity. Policy tailwind (US IIJA, EU RePowerEU/Connecting Europe Facility) plus hard physical necessity make this a multi-decade structural trend.

sub_themes.name: Grid Modernization
sub_themes.definition: Contractors and equipment makers modernizing aging transmission and distribution grids.

sub_themes.name: Water Utility Infrastructure
sub_themes.definition: Water utility pipe, pump and treatment infrastructure renewal.

sub_themes.name: Transport Infrastructure
sub_themes.definition: Rail, road and bridge construction and engineering for transport infrastructure renewal.

trends.name: Resource Scarcity & Producer-Concentration Diversification
trends.thesis: A cross-cutting trend (distinct from the commodity-specific trends above): buyers are actively diversifying critical-mineral and strategic-material supply chains (rare earths, lithium, cobalt) away from single-country concentration risk after export-control shocks (e.g. China rare-earth export licensing). The investable angle is diversification/substitution capacity, not the concentrated incumbent producers themselves.

scarcity.risk: Export-license control gives a single country a chokepoint over magnet-grade rare earths

sub_themes.name: Rare-Earth Separation Outside China
sub_themes.definition: Rare-earth mining and separation/refining capacity being built outside China to diversify magnet-grade supply.

sub_themes.name: Lithium Extraction Diversification
sub_themes.definition: Lithium extraction and processing capacity diversifying supply away from concentrated incumbent sources.

sub_themes.name: Battery-Material Recycling
sub_themes.definition: Recovery of critical battery materials (lithium, cobalt, nickel) from end-of-life batteries as a supply-diversification substitute.

trends.name: Water Pollution & Treatment
trends.thesis: Long-term structural underinvestment in water treatment (PFAS remediation, aging municipal systems, agricultural runoff) combined with tightening regulation (EU and US PFAS limits) is a slow but durable capex trend for treatment technology, monitoring, and utility infrastructure spend.

sub_themes.name: PFAS Remediation & Monitoring
sub_themes.definition: Technology and services for detecting and removing PFAS ('forever chemicals') from water supplies.

sub_themes.name: Municipal Water Treatment Equipment
sub_themes.definition: Equipment and systems for municipal water and wastewater treatment plant renewal.

sub_themes.name: Agricultural Runoff & Monitoring
sub_themes.definition: Precision-agriculture and monitoring technology reducing agricultural runoff pollution.

trends.name: Heating & Cooling Transition
trends.thesis: Heat pump adoption (electrification of heating, EU F-Gas and building efficiency regulation) plus rising cooling demand from both climate warming and AI-driven data-center growth make heating/cooling equipment and refrigerant-transition suppliers a durable, policy-reinforced trend.

sub_themes.name: Heat Pump Manufacturing
sub_themes.definition: Manufacturing of residential and commercial heat pumps replacing fossil-fuel heating systems.

sub_themes.name: Refrigerant Transition
sub_themes.definition: Low-GWP refrigerant development and the equipment transition away from high-GWP refrigerants under F-Gas regulation.

sub_themes.name: Data-Center & Commercial Cooling
sub_themes.definition: Commercial and data-center cooling equipment addressing rising cooling demand from climate warming and AI data centers.

trends.name: Climate-Driven Relocation
trends.thesis: Sea-level rise, wildfire risk, and heat-stress migration are beginning to shift real-estate demand, insurance pricing, and municipal infrastructure spend toward climate-resilient regions. Still early-stage/emerging as an investable trend — most evidence today is insurance repricing and municipal adaptation budgets rather than clear relocation-driven asset flows, so this entry is deliberately conservative (status=emerging, no scarcity block) pending stronger signal.

sub_themes.name: Climate-Resilient Real Estate & Insurance Repricing
sub_themes.definition: Insurance and reinsurance repricing of climate risk and real-estate demand shifting toward climate-resilient regions.

sub_themes.name: Municipal Adaptation Infrastructure
sub_themes.definition: Engineering and infrastructure spend for municipal climate adaptation (flood defense, wildfire mitigation, heat resilience).
